sections.markdown:
## Vehicle preparation, traction and expressway safety

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
The handbook's safety guidance consists of general statements; the driver must assess the actual circumstances rather than treat the list as instructions for every possible situation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Check tire pressure with a gauge against the vehicle's door-label recommendation and adjust pressure to that recommendation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Inspect tires for wear and damage monthly and before a long trip. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
When parked on a street, enter from the curb side if possible. If entry must be from traffic's side, wait until it can be done safely without interfering with passing traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Have the keys ready, approach while facing traffic, and adjust the seat and mirrors before beginning the trip. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Check that passengers are properly seated without blocking the view, and have everyone fasten the belt before starting. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
Before entering traffic, check for hazards, bicycles and pedestrians, signal appropriately and move out cautiously. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
Good driving posture improves the view and vehicle control. Keep both hands on the wheel except while safely performing another driving task. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
The handbook gives a general steering grip of left hand at 9 and right at 3 on a clock face, while noting some manufacturers recommend 8 and 4 for airbag-equipped vehicles. Use the vehicle maker's guidance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
Avoid heavy fog if possible. If driving is necessary, reduce speed and use low beams because high-beam glare makes fog visibility worse. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A01
Slow further in fog when another vehicle's headlights or taillights become visible, because its distance can be hard to judge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A01
The handbook instructs drivers not to travel through fog with parking lights or hazard flashers on. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A01
Hydroplaning occurs when standing water separates a tire from the roadway, reducing the tire's ability to steer, accelerate or brake. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A01
If hydroplaning begins, release the accelerator and let the vehicle slow. Good tire tread and lower speed on water-covered pavement help prevent it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A01
A skid occurs when tire grip is lost. Slick pavement and abrupt steering or braking can make a skid more likely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A01
The handbook advises releasing the accelerator if a skid begins and using only light braking after control returns; steering technique requires the conditions and vehicle to be considered. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A01
During the first half hour of rain, water mixing with road oil and other material makes the surface particularly slippery. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A01
Curves require extra care, particularly on slick pavement. Advisory curve-speed signs identify a recommended reduction that may be below the regular posted limit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=39]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
Reduce speed before a curve. If already too fast within it, avoid a forceful brake application; release the accelerator, brake carefully and continue steering within the lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A02
If the vehicle leaves the pavement, stay calm, release the accelerator, grip the wheel firmly and avoid sudden hard braking or an immediate sharp return. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A02
After leaving the road, let speed decrease, check traffic and choose a safe place to merge back. Stop completely first if necessary. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A02
After a sudden tire rupture, hold the wheel firmly and release the accelerator; use light braking only if necessary and safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A02
Following a blowout, wait until the vehicle has slowed substantially before moving onto the shoulder. If it has already swerved off the road, let it stop rather than jerking back onto the pavement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A02
In winter conditions, use appropriate snow tires or chains only in accordance with the vehicle, tire and chain manufacturers' instructions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A02
Remove snow and ice from all vehicle windows before driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A02
When safe, gently assess winter traction with light braking and small steering adjustments. Avoid abrupt braking, reduce speed gradually before turns or stops and increase following space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A02
Before winter travel, check the battery, cooling system, washer fluid, wipers, defrosters, tires and floor mats, and plan the route and necessary supplies. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A02
Carbon monoxide from a vehicle is colorless, odorless and dangerous. Do not run the engine in a garage or drive with a defective exhaust system. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A02
Avoid leaving a parked vehicle running with its windows closed, including when using its heater or air conditioning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=40]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A03
Do not turn an ignition into the steering-lock position while moving, because a steering lock can prevent steering. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A03
Leave enough following distance to stop safely if the vehicle ahead suddenly slows or stops. The handbook's reference-point method uses a count of about 2 seconds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A03
Increase following space beyond the ordinary reference-point interval at night and in bad weather, construction or heavy traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A03
Stopping distance depends on speed, the driver's reaction, pavement, tires, chassis, brakes and wind; a chart is only a guide rather than a guarantee. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A03
Higher impact speed increases collision force. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=41]

Misconceptions: A stopping chart or a general water-speed example cannot guarantee traction; the manufacturer's vehicle-specific guidance remains relevant.
Mnemonic: Prepare, observe, leave space, slow smoothly.
Glossary: Hydroplaning is tire separation from the wet road; a gore is the marked convergence area between lanes; an acceleration lane supports joining traffic.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Vehicle-specific emergency methods, medical response, emissions eligibility and toll-lane policies remain unresolved review work.

Carbon-monoxide symptoms and artificial-respiration instructions are withheld for current clinical/safety review; no medical treatment is authored.
Image-based stopping-distance and building-height comparisons, the emergency-fire panel with missing context, and image-only diagrams/QR video content are not authored facts.
Accelerator-jam, brake-failure and wet-brake intervention sequences require modern vehicle-specific safety review and are withheld rather than generalized.
Diverging-diamond performance, delay reductions and promotional claims are withheld; no universal design outcome is asserted.
